subject.title: Gateway restart drops queued and in-flight inbound messages

question: Should OpenClaw make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82572 the canonical path for this issue, choose a narrower drain-only mitigation, or wait for a broader channel ingress/catch-up design?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but the durable fix changes runtime state ownership and message replay semantics, so maintainers need to choose the product and architecture boundary before new repair work starts.

options.title: Advance the SQLite recovery PR
options.body: Use the shared-SQLite followup queue recovery approach as the canonical fix path after review, proof, and merge safety are satisfied.

options.title: Limit scope to drain-only mitigation
options.body: Prioritize flushing/draining in-process queues before restart and leave durable replay or downtime catch-up for separate issues.

options.title: Hold for broader channel catch-up
options.body: Treat this issue as part of a larger per-channel durable ingress and missed-message recovery design before landing followup-only persistence.

recommendation.title: Advance the SQLite recovery PR
recommendation.body: Use the shared-SQLite followup queue recovery approach as the canonical fix path after review, proof, and merge safety are satisfied.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged restart-drain work and related gateway lifecycle context make this the strongest available routing owner for the architecture choice.
